answer.summary: Jag Duggal says companies entering an established market should avoid settling for a slightly better, incremental offering; they should try to reinvent the category with a fundamentally different experience.

sections.heading: Mistake to avoid
sections.content: Don’t enter an established market with only a “bit better” offering or incremental differentiation. Duggal says companies should try to reinvent the category even when they are not creating an entirely new one. As an example, Nubank entered Brazil’s established Consignado lending market with a direct-to-consumer model instead of middlemen and significantly lower pricing.
